```{r}
library(BiHeat)
```

## Two matrices, one plot

BiHeat draws a heatmap where each cell is split along a diagonal. The
upper triangle encodes one matrix; the lower triangle encodes another.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
species   <- LETTERS[1:6]
sites     <- letters[1:8]
observed  <- matrix(runif(48),  6, 8, dimnames = list(species, sites))
predicted <- observed + matrix(rnorm(48, sd = 0.15), 6, 8,
                               dimnames = list(species, sites))

biheat(observed, predicted)
```

## The lifecycle

`biheat()` is the one-shot entry point. Under the hood it runs a small
three-stage lifecycle that you can use directly when you want to inspect
or compose the paired object:

```{r}
clutch <- breed(observed, predicted)
clutch
```

`breed()` aligns the two matrices on overlapping dimnames and computes
comparison statistics. `incubate()` adds rendering options. `plot()`
draws.

```{r}
breed(observed, predicted) |>
  incubate(scale = "shared", split = "up") |>
  plot()
```

`incubate()` calls are additive — every call layers new options on top
of the existing config:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
breed(observed, predicted) |>
  incubate(scale = "shared") |>
  incubate(split = "up") |>
  plot()
```

## Verbs

A handful of verbs operate clutch-in / clutch-out:

```{r}
breed(observed, predicted) |>
  switch_sides() |>     # swap which is upper / lower
  straighten() |>       # flip the diagonal
  bothways() |>         # toggle separate <-> shared scale
  plot()
```

`comes_out()` pulls the tidy data back out of a clutch or a rendered
ggplot:

```{r}
breed(observed, predicted) |> comes_out() |> head()
```

## Separate vs. shared scales

By default each side gets its own colour scale (`scale = "separate"`),
which is appropriate when the two matrices measure different things.
When the two matrices live on the same scale, use `scale = "shared"` so
cross-triangle comparisons are meaningful.

```{r}
biheat(observed, predicted, scale = "shared")
```

## Custom palettes

`palettes()` bundles a pair of gradient palettes:

```{r}
biheat(
  observed, predicted,
  palettes = palettes(c("white", "darkorange", "darkred"),
                      c("white", "steelblue",  "navy"))
)
```

## Status

Milestone 2 (this version): full lifecycle (`breed`/`incubate`/`plot`),
verbs operate on clutch objects, `biheat()` as sugar over the
lifecycle. Legend composition (split-tile glyph + paired gradient bars)
and the `geom_biheat()` layer follow in the next milestone.
